question: to the Commission Michalis Hadjipantela (PPE) Subject:

The Commission has already acknowledged that quarrying activities in the occupied areas of Cyprus do not adhere to EU environmental, health and safety regulations, resulting in serious environmental degradation. The Commission’s Directorate-General for Regional and Urban Policy further confirmed in August 2025 that neither the Republic of Cyprus nor the Commission can verify, monitor or enforce compliance with environmental and safety standards in the occupied north. Despite this, no enforcement action has been taken. The Pentadaktylos mountain range is subject to ongoing uncontrolled extraction. Quarry operators in the Republic of Cyprus bear the full burden of EU regulatory compliance, creating a distortion of competition. The imminent opening of new crossing points risks increasing the flow of non-compliant aggregates. 1.

Given the Commission’s admission that it cannot verify compliance with Article 4(1) of Regulation (EC) No 866/2004, does it consider that the legal conditions for permitting aggregates to cross the Green Line are met?
What concrete enforcement steps does the Commission intend to take to tackle the unfair competition faced by economic operators working in areas controlled by the Republic?
Does the Commission intend to make the provision of support to the Turkish Cypriot community conditional on compliance to ensure that EU rules are not violated by those receiving it?
answer: on behalf of the European Commission (22.5.2026) The Commission would like to refer to its position, as already detailed in the replies to written questions E-002402/20251 E-001687/20242 and E-2244/20173. The Commission is aware of the quarrying activities in the Pentadaktylos mountains and continues to follow developments closely. It regularly engages with the Turkish Cypriot community to stress the importance of applying appropriate conservation measures and protect this environmentally sensitive area, as well as facilitating the alignment of legal frameworks with the EU environmental standards. The allegations concerning non-compliance by individual quarrying operators cannot be confirmed or refuted by the Commission. The principles of good administration preclude the adoption of restrictive measures in the absence of substantiated evidence. All goods traded across the Green Line must comply with the requirements of the EU acquis concerning their placement on the EU market4. Pursuant to Protocol 10 of the 2003 Act of Accession5, the EU acquis in the areas of the Republic of Cyprus in which the government of the Republic of Cyprus does not exercise effective control is suspended. The Commission will continue to support environmental protection and the preservation of Cyprus’ sensitive natural areas. Moreover, it remains fully committed to a comprehensive settlement of the Cyprus issue to the benefit of all Cypriots.
